title: Automated Control Artifact Citation Generator for SOC 2 / ISO Evidence Packs
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Problem: Auditors and internal teams spend significant time verifying that collected artifacts actually map to the asserted control in SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reports. Current evidence bundles are a mix of static exports and ad-hoc notes; they lack consistent citations, canonical artifact identifiers, and machine-readable provenance. This increases time-to-audit, causes repeated follow-ups, and makes automated attestation pipelines brittle.

Goal: Build an Automated Control Artifact Citation Generator (ACACG) that: (1) maps control IDs to canonical evidence types and retention windows, (2) generates persistent citations for artifacts collected by our collectors (logs, snapshots, access records, config exports), including content fingerprints and storage locations, (3) produces both human-readable citations for auditor packs and machine-readable manifests (JSON-LD) that feed the evidence orchestration pipeline.

Scope: MVP will support a core subset of SOC 2 common criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A controls related to access, logging, configuration management, and data residency. The generator will integrate with collectors exposed by ENG (log-harvest proxy, residency sampler) and output citations into the evidence vault used by Dedicated/Private customers.

Success metrics: reduce auditor follow-up tickets by 60% for pilot customers, end-to-end evidence assembly time reduced from days to hours, and 100% of generated citations validated by internal compliance team during pilot.

Non-goals: This MVP will not attempt full natural-language mapping from policy wording; that is a follow-on. It will not replace manual attestation but will significantly reduce friction for automated aggregation and reviewer validation.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each supported control maps to at least one canonical evidence type and a standardized citation schema.

AC2: The generator emits a machine-readable manifest (JSON-LD) containing: control_id, artifact_id (GUID), content_fingerprint (sha256), storage_uri, collector_id, collection_timestamp, retention_policy_id.
AC3: Generated citations are attached to evidence bundles in the vault and surfaced in Console evidence previews with a stable permalink.
AC4: Pilot customers (2) validate citation-to-artifact traceability for at least 90% of sampled controls.
AC5: System logs an auditable provenance trail; tamper-evidence provided via signed manifests (KMS/HSM key reference).
AC6: Automated tests cover mapping logic, fingerprint generation, and manifest schema compliance.
design_notes:
We will adopt a compact citation schema inspired by academic citation and software SBOM patterns: control_id::artifact_type::artifact_guid::sha256::storage_uri::collector_version. For machine manifests we will use JSON-LD to ease integration with downstream orchestrators. Retention_policy_id will reference our existing retention catalog (release runtime-1.18 retention table). Consider using time-stamped signing (KMS) to provide tamper evidence and to support long-lived attestations.

Tradeoffs: Embedding full artifact metadata increases manifest size but improves auditability; for large binary artifacts we will emit a pointer + fingerprint rather than inline content. We prioritized deterministic GUID generation (collector_name + timestamp + fingerprint) to avoid duplicates across collectors.

UX: Console will show a citation card with verifier-friendly fields (control summary, artifact preview, fingerprint, download link, signed manifest status). Exported auditor packs will contain both the human summary and zipped machine manifests.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize control->artifact mapping table with Compliance; design citation schema and JSON-LD context.
Week 2: Implement generator library (service) that accepts collector payloads and emits signed manifests; unit tests for fingerprinting and schema validation.
Week 3: Integrate with ENG collectors (log-harvest proxy, residency-evidence sampler) and run end-to-end ingestion tests in staging.
Week 4: Console integration — evidence preview card, permalink, and export flow; pilot with two customers and compliance team review.
Week 5: Iterate on feedback, add retention-policy enforcement hooks and manifest signing via KMS/HSM, finalize docs and runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Collectors produce inconsistent metadata causing mapping failures. Mitigation: Add strict schema validation and fallback heuristics; surface mapping failures as tickets with suggested remediation.
Risk: Signing manifests adds KMS latency. Mitigation: Batch-sign manifests asynchronously and mark pending state in manifest until signature available; ensure retry logic.
Risk: Storage URIs differ across Dedicated/Private deployments. Mitigation: Use abstract storage_uri namespace in manifests plus a deployment-specific resolver in the evidence vault.
